name: Oregon
keyNotes: No post-sale redemption — buyer takes clean title
2025 ORS 312.510 update — verify current county procedures
summary: Oregon requires 3 years delinquency before county takes deed, then 2 years county hold before auction. Opening bids set at 80% of assessed value. Statute: ORS §312.060.
typeWhy: Oregon sells the property deed outright after a 3-year delinquency period. There is no post-sale redemption. ORS §312.060.
rateWhy: Oregon is a deed state with no statutory interest rate. Opening bids are set at 80% of assessed value, limiting deep-discount opportunity. ORS §312.060.
notBeginnerReason: 80% of assessed value minimum bid, 3 years delinquency + 2 years county hold, virtually no below-market opportunity.
beginnerTip: Oregon is not recommended for investors seeking below-market deals. The 80% minimum makes it impractical.
risks: 80% minimum of assessed value leaves minimal margin
5-year total cycle (3-year delinquency + 2-year county hold) is the longest effective cycle
ddExtra: Verify the county's assessed value vs. market value before bidding
Check for environmental or wetlands designations
Calculate whether the 80% minimum leaves any workable margin

steps: Contact the county tax collector — oregon.gov/dor for county directory
Request the upcoming auction schedule and property list
Register per county instructions — most are in-person
Be prepared for opening bids near 80% of assessed value

tylerCompliance.summary: Status pending — monitoring for legislative action.
tylerCompliance.details: This state compliance with Tyler v. Hennepin County (2023) is currently being monitored. Aurigen tracks legislative updates, pending bills, and court decisions that affect tax sale surplus requirements. Check back for updates.

process.delinquencyTrigger: 3 years from first date of delinquency (May 16 of tax year)
process.interest: 1.333% per month (16% annualized) on delinquent taxes — accrues monthly on 16th
process.foreclosureList: County tax collector prepares annual foreclosure list within 2 months of delinquency date
process.publication: August — published in local newspaper + 5% publication penalty assessed
process.applicationForJudgment: County Counsel files application for General Judgment with Circuit Court
process.redemptionAfterJudgment: Owner or interested party may redeem: 2 years from date of General Judgment
process.endOfRedemption: Notice sent before redemption expiration. After 2 years — county gets absolute title.
process.auction: County auctions property. Buildable or >$15K value: Sheriff's Sale. Otherwise: private negotiated sale.

auction.platform: GovEase / Bid4Assets / PublicSurplus / county sheriff auction / oral auction — varies by county
auction.buildable: Buildable lots or value >$15K: must be sold at Sheriff's Sale (public auction)
auction.nonBuildable: Non-buildable or value ≤$15K: county may sell via private negotiated sale

otc.name: County Surplus Property / Private Sale
otc.trigger: No bid at Sheriff's Sale OR non-buildable property
otc.process: Contact county property management office. Complete Surplus Property Purchase Inquiry form.
otc.note: Columbia County confirmed: non-buildable lots available via private sale

subTax.name: N/A — Oregon is deed foreclosure state

redemption.period: 2 years from date of General Judgment (not from delinquency date)
redemption.process: Pay all years in judgment + interest + costs + penalties to county tax collector
redemption.afterJudgment: County sends end-of-redemption notice before expiration. Certified funds required.
redemption.note: Deschutes example: 2023 tax delinquency → eligible foreclsoure May 16 2026 → judgment → 2-year redemption runs to ~mid-2028

deedPath.name: Sheriff's Deed / County Deed
deedPath.titleQuality: No warranty. As-is. Title company may require quiet title for insurance.

surplus.name: Surplus Proceeds
surplus.alert: ⚡ HB 4056 (2024) + 2025 c.475: Oregon enacted Tyler-compliant surplus process. County must publish surplus info on state and county websites. Claimant files within 2 years of sale date.
surplus.process: File Request for Surplus Proceeds with county within 2 years of sale date. Yamhill County confirmed this process.
surplus.orrDorInvolvement: OR DOR hosting county discussions for uniform surplus process per HB 4056
surplus.note: Unclaimed surplus → State Treasurer after claim period (ORS 312.560)

es.summary: Oregón requiere 3 años de morosidad antes de que el condado tome la escritura, luego 2 años de retención antes de la subasta. Las pujas iniciales se establecen al 80% del valor tasado. Estatuto: ORS §312.060.
es.typeWhy: Oregon es un estado de escritura porque los condados venden propiedades embargadas directamente, sin derecho de redención posterior a la venta (ORS §312.060).
es.rateWhy: No se aplica tasa de interés. Las pujas iniciales al 80% del valor tasado limitan las oportunidades de descuento (ORS §312.060).
es.notBeginnerReason: Puja mínima del 80% del valor tasado, 3 años de morosidad + 2 años de retención del condado, prácticamente sin oportunidad por debajo del mercado.
es.beginnerTip: Oregón no se recomienda para inversores que buscan ofertas por debajo del mercado. El mínimo del 80% lo hace impracticable.
risks: Mínimo del 80% del valor tasado deja margen mínimo
Ciclo total de 5 años es el ciclo efectivo más largo
ddExtra: Verifique el valor tasado del condado vs. valor de mercado antes de pujar
Revise designaciones ambientales o de humedales
Calcule si el mínimo del 80% deja algún margen viable

steps: Contacte al recaudador de impuestos del condado — oregon.gov/dor para directorio del condado
Solicite el próximo calendario de subasta y lista de propiedades
Regístrese según instrucciones del condado — la mayoría son en persona
Prepárese para pujas iniciales cerca del 80% del valor tasado
